interactions.prompt: Draft a tracker issue from an observed screenshot without validation or fixes.
Reproduce a screenshot-reported bug in the running UI and prove the visible failure.
Review a screenshot for spacing and overflow, then route any keyboard concern separately.
Audit an existing refresh-token implementation, not a proposed design.
Threat-model a proposed external-send feature before code exists.
Create security audit trajectories across the whole current repository.
Normalize the supplied ticket into behavior examples before planning.
Product intent is missing and no source packet exists; create the smallest durable discovery artifact.
Evidence is validated; decide what should become durable product artifacts before writing them.
The synthesis is approved; write final PRD, persona, requirements, journeys, and scenarios.
Build an agent and skill workflow packet with prompt bank and stop rules.
Track active lanes, dependencies, file ownership, coordination-state/materialization owner, and validation gates.
Write a normal implementation plan with examples and risks, no workflow packet or lane registry.
Compile selected reusable pattern sections, not current branch state.
Orient to branch, dirty files, active lanes, and recent reports, not reusable patterns.
Review a fixed-point diff for standards and spec findings without running tests.
Aggregate commands, tests, functional evidence, review findings, and feature impact into status.
Product behavior is correct but a locator changed; repair the semantic test.
An approved plan identifies the documented contract, failing runtime behavior, and product-code target. Apply the scoped product fix, not a test repair.
Audit a provider-neutral agent architecture without choosing Codex files.
Change Codex custom-agent TOML, skill wiring, config, and validator surfaces.
Turn a repeated workflow into a focused reusable skill package.
Evaluate generated harness scenarios and their JSONL traces; do not repair the harness.
A harness evaluation confirmed a defect; now repair the owning skill and validator.
Create and calibrate new outcome and trajectory judge profiles, anchored rubrics, schemas, and aggregation rules; do not run completed traces yet.
The judge profiles and rubrics are fixed; run them independently on completed harness traces and calculate current accepted coverage.

Classify a one-file typo correction with one bounded obligation and no cross-workline dependency, evidence join, materialization boundary, invalidation relation, partial-repair branch, or revision-sensitive state. Determine whether a Coordination Graph is needed and identify the ordinary planning, permission, review, validation, and closeout obligations that still apply; do not edit anything.

Recompute readiness for a complex lane where N-03 requires accepted N-01 and N-02 plus current human approval. N-01 is accepted, N-02 is still in review, and approval is absent. Return the node state, unmet typed dependencies, and the deterministic resume condition without executing work.

A graph-bound worker has produced its assigned diff, but review and validation evidence do not exist. One actor proposes ACCEPTED while another proposes FAILED. Return the worker's version-bound receipt, proposed transition, treatment of both proposals, and handoff to the authoritative state writer; do not mutate shared lane/Coordination Graph state or the Materialization Queue.

Evaluate a gate that requires command and functional evidence. The command evidence passes, the functional check is BLOCKED, and previously accepted required evidence has since been invalidated. Keep the evidence classes separate and report the gate proposal, node impact, and reopen route.

Assess repair impact after an integrated active-worktree check finds workline B's materialized skill contract incompatible with the graph schema and its evidence is bound to an old input version. Workline A has accepted current evidence and unchanged inputs. A consumer workline depends on B's producer gate and version. Identify the earliest responsible workline, reopened gates, materializations, batches, and consumers, preserved accepted work, and freshness conditions.

An automated check failed on a graph node while the documented product behavior is believed correct. Compare three requested follow-ups: retry the same topology with attempts remaining, add a new consumer-mapping node, and retry after the unchanged-topology maximum is already consumed. Report attempt versus revision effects, blocked or repair states, preserved evidence, and the deterministic escalation route.

Resume a graph-shaped lane after compaction. The saved Current Frontier says N-04 is READY, but authoritative node and gate records show an unresolved join and a newer graph revision. Rehydrate the authoritative state, report projection drift, and return the reconciled frontier, blockers, and next executable node without implementation.

Review a proposed task graph before implementation. A consumer requires its producer to be accepted, while their shared aggregate gate also requires the consumer's evidence; the revision also reuses a superseded node ID and an existing gate ID. Report graph validity, blocking defects, and the revision or repair needed before readiness.

Root is preparing worker dispatch, but required source changes are uncommitted and therefore absent from the proposed HEAD. Decide whether a worktree may be created, and return the dispatch-base evidence, state, and exact condition for safe resumption without modifying the repository.

Plan the next dependency wave after AG-01 is accepted. WL-02, WL-03, and WL-04 have disjoint declared writes, separate thread/branch/worktree identities, one immutable base, per-workline gates, and one root coordination-state/materialization owner. Determine whether they may run concurrently and return dispatch, immutable transport, evidence-join, Materialization Queue, and downstream readiness boundaries.

A request has three canonical worklines with a producer dependency, a shared evidence join, dedicated-worktree materialization, and partial-repair propagation. Decide whether to create a first-class docs/work/graphs/CG-XXX entry, keep lane-local Task Graphs and rich spec definitions in their owners, and make active.md a projection; return graph authority, cutover, and terminal-gate boundaries without editing.

Existing W-101 and W-102 have the same outcome, compatible criteria and write scope, duplicate evidence boundaries, and the same consumers; W-103 is complete with preserved receipts, while active.md still marks it active. Audit current source and inbound references, then return exact duplicate, stale projection, survivor migration, retention, and active-row dispositions before any graph cutover.

Two existing worklines have similar titles but only partially overlapping criteria, different output contracts, and different consumers. A maintainer asks to merge and delete one immediately. Return the comparison matrix, safe disposition, unresolved boundary route, preserved evidence, canonical-survivor status, and graph-cutover decision.

A newly approved request has no existing lane packets or graph. Discover its worklines, criterion ownership, dependencies, validation seams, and initial Coordination Graph applicability; do not perform stale-state reconciliation.

Author an approved product spec with requirements, behavior examples, and acceptance checks. No active execution coordination is requested. Keep Coordination Graph tables out of the generated spec and route execution planning separately.

An accepted workline commit is queued for root-owned materialization into the current active worktree. Return the required dirty-target preflight and a materialization receipt/proposal that applies only allowed paths, preserves unrelated changes, records identical target HEAD before/after plus the resulting combined diff fingerprint, and does not commit, push, clean, reset, or broadly stage; do not mutate the repository in this evaluation.

A queued workline transport changes src/shared.py, but the active worktree already has unexplained unstaged edits to that path plus an unrelated dirty notes.md. Decide the materialization state and return overlap evidence, preservation requirements, deterministic resume route, and receipt proposal without overwriting, cleaning, committing, or staging anything.

Assess a Coordination Graph harness batch bound to target HEAD plus combined diff and versioned catalog, runner, model, environment, and rubrics. One required shard is missing, one required result is stale, and two receipts duplicate the same evidence ID and subject with conflicting results. Return shard completeness, explicit duplicate disposition, evidence-level separation, aggregation result, invalidation, earliest responsible route, and proposed gate transition; do not run models.

Every dedicated-worktree worker reports local PASS, but their accepted transports have not all been materialized and no integrated active-worktree check binds the current target HEAD plus combined diff. Aggregate the evidence without promoting local receipts, and return materialization, batch, terminal-gate states and the exact acceptance condition.

An integrated batch fails because WL-02 produced a stale contract. WL-01 and WL-04 have accepted evidence with unchanged inputs; WL-03 consumes WL-02. Return the earliest responsible workline, reopened worklines/gates/materializations/batches/consumers, preserved accepted IDs, invalidated versions, bounded repair frontier, and resume condition without restarting the whole graph.

Plan a non-atomic full-stack feature with unresolved interaction states, a changed API contract, backend persistence, frontend implementation, cross-surface wiring, public-start E2E, authorization risk, accessibility, and visual behavior. Produce the graph-fragment disposition ledger, port bindings, actor and skill calls, exact test-strategy resolution requirements, workline boundaries, assurance overlays, emission decision, and terminal evidence join before implementation; do not edit code.

Plan a backend-only internal calculation repair. Product acceptance and API shape are unchanged; no UI, persistence, integration, auth, accessibility, visual, or public-start journey changes. Evaluate reusable graph fragments, select only the smallest applicable obligations and focused tests, justify omitted fragments, and avoid generating frontend, design, E2E, or Coordination Graph state.

The approved plan selected product, contract, backend, frontend, integration, E2E, security, accessibility, and visual fragment instances. Compose them into the smallest workline set: bind requires/provides ports, merge compatible obligations, split only independent ownership and evidence seams, resolve roles/skills/tests/evaluators, reject dangling ports and cycles, and decide lane-local versus Coordination Graph emission without executing work.

Build an agent-and-skill workflow packet from an approved graph-fragment composition ledger. Preserve fragment IDs and versions, port bindings, owning worklines, existing role or authorized-worker resolution, step-level skill calls, tests and evaluator authority, omission reasons, repair handoffs, and graph-emission owner; do not create dynamic agents or active graph state.

Validate an assembled feature graph where backend, frontend, integration, E2E, and accessibility fragments are selected, visual and migration fragments are explicitly not applicable, the backend evidence passes, frontend evidence is current, integration evidence is missing, and a stale visual receipt exists from an older plan. Return the fragment evidence matrix, omit the visual receipt from required inputs, block the terminal join on missing integration evidence, and identify the bounded repair route.
